ranking.note: Raised to P1: it is the category-defining project (in-tree unit test runner) that several other PRs (#35139, #36091) feed into and that removes a recurring build/platform burden.
Raised to P2: adds a genuinely new framework capability (autonomous outbound connections via proxy) that unlocks p2p coverage other tests cannot reach today.
Raised to P2 for consistency with the other CI-signal guards (#36098, #35774): hermeticity enforcement prevents a whole class of flaky, environment-dependent failures.
Moved up: hidden Qt test output means Windows unit test failures are invisible in CI, which is the 'misleading signal' problem this category ranks first.
Moved up: it already exposed a real Windows path-handling bug, so it is signal-producing rather than merely additional coverage.
Moved up: a verbosity-3 benchmark that silently measured verbosity-2 work is a misleading measurement, not just a missing one.
Moved up to sit with the other measured fuzz-throughput wins (#34969, #36121), which have comparable consequence.
Moved up: it fixes a concrete reported failure (#35416) blocking concurrent local CI runs, above pure coverage additions.
Moved up: failure diagnostics work that feeds the #35713 runner overhaul ranks above standalone coverage additions.
Moved up: closely tied to the #35713 runner project and to fail-fast CI log behaviour, so it should be reviewed near it.
Moved down: benchmark fixture modernization is real but deferrable relative to CI-signal and throughput fixes; also entangled with #36254's use of the same fixture.
Moved up: the fuzzer already found an actual coin-selection crash, which outranks purely additive harnesses.
Moved up: it reaches HTTP framing code newly added in #35735 that was previously unreachable by the fuzzer.
Moved up: enabling container invariant checking in existing CI jobs can surface real corruption bugs, more than a single new local test.
Moved down: runner ergonomics/IDE integration, no new coverage or signal, so below coverage and speed items.
Moved down: maintainer backport convenience for an infrequent operation, below items affecting everyday test signal.
Moved down: fixes fixture regeneration on no-wallet builds, a narrow tooling gap compared with the coverage and signal items above.
Moved down: a single targeted benchmark whose value is tied to an unmerged optimization (#27865).
Moved down: purely preventative hardening; the card states no existing test hits the broken boundaries.
Lowered to P4: reviewers judge fuzzing wallet RPCs without chain state or UTXOs to have very low efficacy, making the claimed coverage gain weakly justified.
Lowered to P4: the author prefers abandoning this approach and the tidy check introduced a witness-dropping bug, so its value in this category is speculative.
Moved up within P4: it removes real compiler warnings and UB risk repo-wide, the strongest of the hygiene items.
Placed last: NACKed as unused in-tree, set nowhere in the repo, and stale; no claim on review attention.

inconsistencies: #35713 (in-tree runner) and #35139 (custom ASSERT/ASSERT_EQ macros) both introduce replacement assertion macros for Boost.Test; they overlap and could produce two competing macro sets. Decide the direction on #35713 first, then land #35139 against it.
#36091 explicitly supplies printer/operator<< logic 'intended for the unit test runner overhaul in #35713' — the two are a chain; reviewing #36091 first is cheap and de-risks #35713.

#32554 (replace the embedded block413567.raw with a runtime block generator) and #36254 (add undo data for block 413567 to the benchmark fixtures) pull the benchmark fixture strategy in opposite directions; settle whether the static block stays before merging both. #32554 also supersedes the earlier #32457.

Three fuzz-throughput PRs overlap in purpose: #36121 (runner-level corpus sharding), #36068 (wallet reuse) and #34969 (scriptpubkeyman harness). #36121 is runner-wide and should be reviewed first; the other two are independent of it.
#35442 bundles and depends on #35433 (deprecating the replaceable RPC arguments); it cannot be evaluated on its own until that lands.

#36074 (scripted-diff adding util/check.h includes) and #36087 (AssertUnreachable plus two linters) both mechanically rewrite assertion usage across the same test/bench/fuzz files; they will conflict with each other and should be sequenced deliberately.
#35356 depends on fixing the wallet_signer path-quoting bug it exposed; that underlying bug fix, not the CI change, is the substantive work here.
result.notes: This category has one clear anchor project (#35713) with two satellite PRs, a small P2 tier of CI-signal and high-risk-coverage work, and a long P3 tail of fuzz harnesses, benchmarks and coverage additions that are genuinely interchangeable in value. I deliberately promoted signal-restoring CI changes (#36024, #35356, #36254) above purely additive coverage, per the category's stated ordering, and pushed disputed-efficacy or author-abandoned work into P4.
